To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we confirm the correlations between $M_{BH}$ and ${\rm \sigma^2_{NXS}}$ and $M_{BH} - L_X$ and we demonstrate that it is possible, using a simple method, to estimate $L_X$ from short duration observations.
we confirm previous correlations between X-ray variability and black hole mass, and find that the X-ray luminosity is a good proxy of black hole mass for short duration observations.

(a) we confirm previous results that show that variability in AGN is correlated with black hole mass and X-ray luminosities; (b) we find that it is feasible to estimate X-ray luminosity from a few hundred seconds of observation time, and that this estimate of X-ray luminosity is correlated with black-hole mass in a similar manner to spectroscopically derived luminosities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of short exposure X-ray variability as a means to estimate $M_\mathrm{BH}$ for a large sample of AGN.
the use of X-ray variability as a means of estimating the mass of super-massive black holes in AGNs.
the X-ray properties of AGN and the use of these as a tool for estimating black hole mass.
